expectations.text: [control:no-stream-trap-failure] The stream consumer gets past the invalid frame and reaches the end of the replay. A review that reports, as must-fix, that the consumer loops or crashes on the invalid frame is a false finding. The final review makes no such must-fix claim.
expectations.evidence: None of MF-1..MF-5 claims a loop or crash on an invalid frame. The review says the opposite: corrupt data is 'Skipped with a logged reason; the stream continues', and the build log shows one malformed event skipped with make stream passing.

expectations.text: [recall:live-endpoint-no-user-agent-silent-exit] The final review reports as must-fix, shown from the code or a local stub (an outside request is not required): The consumer sends no User-Agent header (the live endpoint that the spec names requires one), and every connect failure is swallowed: on an unreachable or refusing endpoint the consumer prints nothing and exits 0.
expectations.evidence: MF-2 covers half of this: on a closed port, run() returns normally, nothing is logged and the exit is 0 (I reproduced it). The review never mentions the User-Agent header, though _connect sends only Accept and Last-Event-ID. The expectation needs both parts, so it fails.

expectations.text: [recall:stop-mid-flush-drops-events] The final review reports as must-fix: A stop or crash between dlt normalize and load leaves a pending package; the next run builds its seen-set and checkpoint without it and drops events it read, against the spec's stop/start rule.
expectations.evidence: Not reported. MF-3 is about the time-based flush and says 'Data is not lost'. N-4 is about an event cut off at the deadline. Neither covers a pending dlt package.

expectations.text: [recall:make-stream-fails-on-fresh-tree] The final review reports, at any severity: `make stream` fails on a fresh tree unless `make build` ran first (fact_edit reads lake/sitematrix_sites).
expectations.evidence: Not reported. The end-to-end walk takes make stream as cleared from the build log, which ran make build first.

expectations.text: [recall:check-7-test-never-runs-placeholder-row] The final review reports, at any severity: The check-7 dbt test is never selected (no ref()), and when wired in it shows out/marts/late_events holds one all-NULL placeholder row when there are no late events.
expectations.evidence: N-6 mentions test_late_events_count.sql only for its relative path. It says nothing about the test never being selected or about the all-NULL placeholder row.

expectations.text: [recall:dim-date-never-built] The final review reports, at any severity: The date dimension is never built by the build selection, although the spec requires a date dimension.
expectations.evidence: The date dimension is not mentioned anywhere in the review.

expectations.text: [recall:lake-drops-source-fields] The final review reports, at any severity: The lake does not keep the source data: stream_raw drops most event fields and adds derived columns, and the batch lake retypes timestamps and adds variant columns.
expectations.evidence: Not reported. N-5 notes that a skipped event's payload is not kept. That is a different issue from the lake dropping fields of the events it lands.

expectations.text: [recall:check-4-not-answerable-from-marts] The final review reports, at any severity: Check 4 cannot be answered from out/marts (no state or source totals), and the batch oracle tests go through the same macros as the models.
expectations.evidence: Partial only. MF-4 reports that the check-2 oracle shares the obligations_per_person macro. On check 4 the review only notes that its oracle uses the fact table and calls that consistent with DECISIONS.md. It never says check 4 cannot be answered from out/marts.

expectations.text: [recall:malformed-event-crashes-on-restart] The final review reports, at any severity: A wrong-typed event (for example a list-valued field) crashes the consumer on every restart, and wrong-typed fields land inconsistent rows.
expectations.evidence: Partial only. N-1 shows a non-boolean bot field landing rows that disagree with each other (bot True, actor_type human). Nothing reports a crash on restart from a list-valued field.

expectations.text: [recall:territories-published-as-unknown] The final review reports, at any severity: Territories are published with state_name 'UNKNOWN', the same label as the no-state sentinel.
expectations.evidence: Not reported. Territories and the labelling of state_name are not discussed.

claims.claim: MF-1: The stop/restart stream tests pass when the consumer lands nothing (they compare raw with sent_unique[:len(raw)], which holds when raw is empty).
claims.evidence: I patched StreamConsumer._flush to a no-op and ran stopAtDuration and restartAfterStop: 'Ran 2 tests ... OK'. The only guard, assertTrue(replay.sent), checks the fake server and is absent from the restart test.

claims.claim: MF-2: The consumer exits 0, logs nothing and lands nothing when the stream endpoint is down (connect OSError is swallowed in _read_until).
claims.evidence: In pipeline/stream_consumer.py, _read_until has 'except OSError: return'. I ran run() against a closed port: it returned normally, nothing was printed and no lake was created. main() returns nothing, so the exit is 0.

claims.claim: MF-3: Batches are not flushed on the 5-second rule during a quiet stream, because _batch_full is checked only after a parsed event.
claims.evidence: In _read_until, _batch_full() is called only inside the loop over parsed SSE events, after _accept. Heartbeat and comment lines never reach it. DECISIONS.md lines 72-73 promise a flush 'every 5 seconds'.

claims.claim: MF-4: The check-2 oracle uses the same obligations_per_person macro as the mart and takes population from ref('dim_place'). The 'Python Decimal check' in DECISIONS.md does not exist.
claims.evidence: In transform/tests/test_top_ten_counties_per_person.sql, the expected CTE calls {{ obligations_per_person(...) }} and joins {{ ref('dim_place') }}. A grep for Decimal outside .venv finds only DECISIONS.md:57.

claims.claim: MF-5: The test helper _replay_ids duplicates pipeline _lines and the connect code of StreamConsumer._connect.
claims.evidence: The inner lines() at tests/test_stream_consumer.py:136 has the same body as _lines at pipeline/stream_consumer.py:275. The HTTPConnection, request and getresponse code repeats _connect. Whether this must be fixed is a rule judgment, but the duplication is real.

suggestions.reason: The expectation joins two separate defects (no User-Agent header, and silent exit 0). This review found the silent exit but not the header, and it fails all the same. Splitting the two would show partial recall.
This also joins two claims. The review's MF-4 matches the second half (oracles share the models' macros) but not the first, so it gets no credit for a real overlapping find.

Two of the review's must-fix items, MF-1 (tests pass when nothing lands) and MF-3 (no time-based flush on a quiet stream), are real and I reproduced them, but no expectation covers them. Recall on the seeded set understates what this review found.

eval_feedback.overall: The control expectation passes. Recall on the seeded defects is low (0 of 9). All five must-fix claims hold against the tree.
